newsitem.title: INDIA: India trade seeks to boost area under Basmati rice.
newsitem.headline: India trade seeks to boost area under Basmati rice.

text.p: India's rice trade has urged farmers to increase the area under aromatic Basmati rice cultivation to cash in on surging global demand and high prices, industry officials said on Thursday.
"We have urged the states to increase the area under Basmati rice cultivation," Anil Adlakha, executive director of the All India Rice Exporters Association (AIREA), told Reuters.
Industry officials said India's Basmati rice output in the 1996/97 (April-March) season fell to about 730,000 tonnes from 850,000 tonnes in the previous season.
"The shortfall in crop and firm global demand has pushed up Basmati rice prices," Mulraj Tanna, a leading Bombay foodgrains exporter, told Reuters.
Trade officials said Indian Basmati rice for export was currently quoted at $1,100 per tonne FOB (free on board), which was about $900 per tonne at the same time last year.
"Basmati rice prices are expected to rise further as domestic availability is less," said Prem Garg, managing director of Shivnathrai Harnarayan, a leading New Delhi foodgrains exporter.
Trade officials said there was robust demand for Basmati rice, mainly from the United States, the Middle East and some European countries.
"Commonwealth of Independent States countries are also showing interest for Basmati rice," Garg said.
Industry officials said Basmati rice exports in the 1996/97 (April-March) season totalled about 450,000 tonnes and exports in the current season were expected to match that.
"Exports will be as good as last year," Adlakha said.

Trade officials said export demand for non-Basmati rice was currently dull due to the end of the season and non-availability of good quality rice, but there was constant demand for parboiled and 100 percent broken variety rice.
The demand for 100 percent broken was mainly from Senegal and for parboiled rice, the demand was mainly from Nigeria and Somalia, industry officials said.
"During the last week there were no new contracts," Garg said. "Only shipments of the past commitments are going on."
Tanna said at least five vessels, each with 12,000 tonnes of rice, were being loaded at different Indian ports for shipment.
Poor export demand for long grain non-Basmati rice had pushed down Indian prices marginally, but prices of parboiled rice had risen slightly on good overseas demand, traders said.
Indian five percent broken non-Basmati rice was quoted at $300-310 FOB, 10 percent at $290-300, 15 percent at $275-285 and 25 percent at $245-255 per tonne, traders said.
Sowing for the new rice crop was in full swing after plentiful monsoon rains, with 70 percent of sowing operations over, industry officials said.
They said it was too early to give a forecast for the next crop. "We hope monsoon rains continue to be good," Adlakha said.
India harvested a rice crop of 80.54 million tonnes in 1996/97 (July-June), up from 79.62 million in the previous year. The government has not made a rice output forecast for 1997/98.
